intro: Looking for an Innovator Founder visa adviser near you usually means you have a business idea you believe in and you want someone local, or easy to reach, who can help you turn it into a successful endorsement application. This visa is for entrepreneurs setting up an innovative, viable and scalable business in the UK, and the adviser's role is to guide you through endorsement and the application that follows. We can introduce you to a suitable UK immigration adviser who will quote you directly, with fees on application.
need_heading: What people searching for an Innovator visa adviser near me usually need
need_lead: Most people behind this search are at the start of a serious business venture and want expert help with the endorsement stage.

You are unsure which approved endorsing body fits your sector and want advice on how to approach the right one.
You have already been refused endorsement or a visa and want a professional to look at what went wrong before you try again.
You need to understand how the Innovator Founder route differs from other work visas and whether it suits your plans.
You want an adviser you can meet or speak to easily, which is often why people add near me to their search.
context_heading: The key thing to understand about Innovator Founder visa advice
context: Giving immigration advice in the UK is regulated: it is a criminal offence to advise unless the adviser is registered with the Immigration Advice Authority (formerly the OISC) at the right level, or is a solicitor, barrister or chartered legal executive authorised by their own regulator. Before you share business plans or pay anyone, check the IAA's adviser finder or the SRA register. IAA advisers are registered at levels that limit what they can handle, so ask what level they hold and whether it covers endorsement work.

Endorsement from an approved body is required before you can apply, and the quality of your business plan matters enormously. The endorsing body will assess whether your idea is innovative, viable and scalable, and check-in meetings follow once you are endorsed. iComply does not give immigration advice itself; we simply introduce you to a regulated professional who can.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Describe your business idea briefly and say which sector it sits in.
Say whether you have already approached an endorsing body or been endorsed.
Mention any previous visa refusals or endorsement refusals, as these affect the advice you need.
Explain whether you are applying from inside or outside the UK.
Say whether you would prefer to meet an adviser in person locally or are happy to work remotely.
Note any deadlines or start dates you are working towards so the adviser can judge availability.
questions: Are you registered with the Immigration Advice Authority, and at what level?
Does your registration cover Innovator Founder endorsement and application work?
How do you approach the business plan and the endorsement stage?
Which endorsing bodies have you worked with for ideas like mine?
What do the check-in meetings after endorsement involve?
How will you keep me informed as the application progresses?

faqs.q: Do I need an adviser to apply for the Innovator Founder visa?
faqs.a: You can apply yourself, but endorsement depends on a strong business plan and many people use a regulated adviser to prepare it. An adviser can also help you choose an endorsing body and avoid common mistakes.

faqs.q: Why does the search say near me?
faqs.a: People often want an adviser they can meet face to face or reach easily. Many immigration advisers work remotely as well, so it is worth asking whether location matters for your case.

faqs.q: How do I check that an adviser is allowed to help me?
faqs.a: Check the Immigration Advice Authority's adviser finder or the SRA register before sharing documents or paying. Ask what level the adviser is registered at and whether it covers your matter.

faqs.q: What happens after I am endorsed?
faqs.a: You apply for the visa, and once you are in the UK the endorsing body holds check-in meetings with you. Your adviser can explain what those involve and what you need to show.
